name: a wrapping object names the table, a trailing _id is the key
out: UPDATE sys_menu SET menu_name = 'Home', path = '/home' WHERE menu_id = 1;

name: plain object gets the placeholder table
out: UPDATE table_name SET path = '/home' WHERE menu_id = 1;

name: an exact id beats a trailing _id, wherever it appears
out: UPDATE table_name SET menu_id = 1, name = 'x' WHERE id = 7;

name: the first trailing _id wins when there are several
out: UPDATE table_name SET name = 'x', parent_id = 2 WHERE menu_id = 1;

name: with no id at all the first key is the key
out: UPDATE table_name SET name = 'x' WHERE code = 'A1';

name: set order is the order in the input
out: UPDATE table_name SET z = 2, a = 3 WHERE id = 1;

name: quotes are doubled in the where clause as well as the set
out: UPDATE table_name SET name = 'a''b' WHERE code = 'O''B';

name: null and booleans are keywords, not strings
out: UPDATE table_name SET note = NULL, ok = FALSE WHERE id = 1;

name: numbers are written exactly as they appear
out: UPDATE table_name SET n = 1.50 WHERE id = 9007199254740993;

name: a nested value becomes compact json in a string
out: UPDATE table_name SET meta = '{"a":1,"b":[2,3]}' WHERE id = 1;

name: a run of capitals is one word
out: UPDATE table_name SET http_status = 200 WHERE user_id = 1;

name: rejects one key, because nothing is left to set
rejects an array, because a batch is not one row
